name: MulticallWithETH
rootCause: The victim contract (0x3DA0...92046) exposed a public multicall-style function (selector 0xc9586258, taking an array of Call{target, callData, value, allowFailure}) that executes arbitrary low-level calls on behalf of the contract without any access control or sender validation. Because the multicall executes calls from the victim contract's own context (and the contract held approvals/allowances), an attacker could craft a Call invoking transferFrom (selector 0x23b872dd) to move USDC from an approving address (0xfb0D...A581) to the attacker. The attacker simply called the unprotected multicall with a transferFrom payload, draining ~10K USDT/USDC worth of funds. The root cause is an unrestricted arbitrary-call/multicall entrypoint that anyone can use to make the contract perform privileged token transfers. Vulnerable code snippet: Attack Tx: https://bscscan.com/tx/0x6da7be6edf3176c7c4b15064937ee7148031f92a4b72043ae80a2b3403ab6302 Analysis: Attack Tx (BscScan)
